Docs / AeoScript / Attributes
Attributes 
Add named values to Cells and Actors.
Read and write
const door = cell.get(12345)
if door != nil {
debug.log(door.attributes["locked"])
door.attributes["locked"] = true
}
Authored Cell Attributes support numbers, booleans, and strings. Set their saved values in the editor.
Temporary changes
Cell Attribute changes during Play are temporary. Assigning nil removes the temporary override and restores the saved value.
Use Save data for progress that must survive a game restart.
See Cell properties and Actor properties.

Docs / AeoScript / Audio
Audio 
Play sounds from AudioEmitter Cells.
Find an emitter
Give the AudioEmitter Cell a name and choose its sound in the editor.
const speakers = find("DoorSound")
if basket.len(speakers) > 0 {
speakers[0].sound.play()
}
proj.find() searches Actors, so use a Cell lookup for an AudioEmitter Cell.
Control playback
The sound handle has play(), pause(), and stop(). Read playing to check playback. Set looped and volume to control it.
These controls affect the current Play session. A missing emitter must be handled before reading sound.
See the Audio reference for the properties and methods.

entries.title: Baskets
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Baskets
Baskets 
Store values in order.
Create a basket
const items = ["Sword", "Potion"]
debug.log(items[0])
Indices start at 0. This prints Sword.
Shared contents
Assigning a basket does not copy it. Both variables refer to the same contents.
const a = [1, 2]
const b = a
b[0] = 99
debug.log(a[0])
This prints 99. Use basket.clone(a) for a separate outer copy. Nested baskets are still shared.
Change or search a basket
basket.insert(items, "Map")
const index = basket.find(items, "Potion")
if index != nil {
debug.log(items[index])
}
Basket search finds a value inside a basket. It does not search World objects.
Reference
See the Basket API for insertion, removal, sorting, copying, and freezing. Mutation of a frozen basket reports an error.
PreviousControl flowNextMaps

entries.title: Script bindings
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Script bindings
Script bindings 
Attach a script to a specific object.
Bind by ID
A binding connects a script path to an authored Cell ID or Actor ID. The object name is not the binding key.
Two objects may share a name while keeping separate script bindings.
Choose the attachment
Use a Cell binding for a Cell script. Attach a Module beneath an Actor for Actor behavior. See Actors and Modules.
Top-level startup code does not require an entity declaration. Lifecycle functions require the matching attachment; declaring on_ready() alone does not make it startup code.
Missing bindings
If Output reports that no binding exists, check the target ID and script path. Renaming an object should not require switching to a name-based binding.
See Script errors.

entries.title: Cells
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Cells
Cells 
Read and change voxel World objects during Play.
Get a Cell
Use Finding Objects to choose a name or ID lookup.
const block = cell.get(12345)
if block != nil {
block.color = [1, 0.5, 0]
}
Replace 12345 with a Cell ID from your World.
Change a Cell
Visibility, collision, color, and other supported properties can change during Play. Ordinary changes do not rewrite the saved World. They are discarded when Play stops.
Create or delete
cell.new("Block") creates a temporary Cell. cell.delete(handle) removes it from the active World. Deleting an authored Cell during Play is temporary too.
For a complete example, see Create a runtime Cell.
Attributes
Use Attributes for custom named values. See the Cell API for types, properties, and limits.

entries.title: Live Entities
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Live Entities
Live Entities 
Control objects that exist during Play.
Get a live Entity
const enemy = get_entity("Goblin")
if enemy != nil {
enemy.damage(10)
}
No match returns nil. An Entity ID belongs to the runtime. It is not an authored Actor ID.
Position and movement
Use position for a three-number position and velocity for movement. jump(), damage(), heal(), and destroy() act on a valid Entity.
Read grounded to check whether it is on the ground. Select the base animation with animation_name; animation is an animation handle, not a string.
Check validity
if enemy != nil && enemy.is_valid() {
debug.log(enemy.health)
}
Capabilities
An Entity's physics, animation, and appearance handles expose different controls. Appearance-specific controls are not implemented yet.
See the Entity API and Physics API.

entries.title: Entity scripts
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Entity scripts
Entity scripts 
Keep per-object state and respond to lifecycle calls.
Declare an Entity script
entity Counter {
count: number = 0
fn update(dt) {
count += 1
}
}
Bind the script to the object that owns this behavior. Declaring lifecycle functions alone does not attach the script to an object.
Lifecycle
Common functions are on_spawn(), on_ready(), update(dt), and on_destroy(). Use only the ones you need.
Fields keep their values between lifecycle calls. Separate instances keep separate field values.
Choose the right model
Use top-level code for game-wide startup. Use Actor-attached Modules for Actor behavior. An entity declaration and a live Entity handle are different things.
See Live Entities for runtime object controls.

entries.title: Events
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Events
Events 
Let scripts communicate without directly calling each other.
Fire an event
event.fire("enemy_killed", enemy)
The first argument is the event name. Later arguments are values sent with it.
Receive an event
on enemy_killed(enemy) {
debug.log("Enemy defeated:", enemy.name())
}
The handler's name must match the fired event. Events are queued; do not treat event.fire() as a direct function call with a return value.
Event arguments
Pass the values the handler needs. Keep their order the same.
event.fire("score_changed", 25)
on score_changed(amount) {
debug.log("New score:", amount)
}
Contact events
An on_touch callback receives the touching object. It is not limited to the Player.
coin.on_touch = fn(thing) {
const player_entity = get_entity("Player")
if thing != player_entity {
return
}
coin.visible = false
coin.solid = false
}
This fragment assumes coin is already a valid object handle. See Finding Objects. Entity contact callbacks run when contact begins, not on every physics step while contact continues.
Other events
See Input for key presses and Actor navigation for route completion. The Events reference lists call signatures and callback arguments.
PreviousFinding ObjectsNextWaiting
[BETA] marks features newer than the current public release. Current release: 0.8.0.

entries.title: Finding Objects
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Finding Objects
Finding Objects 
Choose a lookup that searches the objects you need.
Choose a lookup
What you need
Use
Result
One authored Actor
proj.find(name)
Actor or nil
All matching Actors
proj.find.all(name)
Basket of Actors
A Cell by name
find(name)
Basket of matching handles
A Cell by ID
cell.get(id)
Cell or nil
A live Entity by name
get_entity(name)
Entity or nil
A live Entity by ID
entity.get(id)
Entity or nil
Player-attached Modules
player.find(name)
Module or nil
A UI control by script key
ui.find(key)
Ui or nil
Find Actors
proj.find() finds Actors. It does not find Cells.
const door = proj.find("Door")
if door != nil {
door.visible = false
}
It searches the project hierarchy and its descendants. No match returns nil. Multiple matches produce a warning and return the first match. Use proj.find.all() when names may be shared.
const enemies = proj.find.all("Enemy")
for enemy in enemies {
debug.log(enemy.id)
}
A folder narrows the search: proj.Dungeon.find("Door") searches that folder and its descendants.
Find Cells
Global find() can find named Cells, including authored Cells. It also searches Actors and live Entities. Its result is always a basket, so check it before indexing.
const matches = find("DoorCell")
if basket.len(matches) > 0 {
const door = matches[0]
door.visible = false
}
Use a distinct Cell name when other object types may share it. No matches returns an empty basket. Global find() remains available as a compatibility lookup; proj.find() is not a replacement for Cell lookup.
If you know a Cell's ID, use cell.get(id). If you need a whole Cell class, use getAllCellsOfClass("Block").
Find live Entities
get_entity("Goblin") finds a live Entity by name. entity.get(id) uses its runtime ID. An Actor ID and an Entity ID are different.
Check for nil before using a lookup result. If the object may have been destroyed later, check is_valid() too.
Find Player Modules
player.find("Inventory") searches Modules attached to the Player. It does not search World Cells or arbitrary Actors. Use player.find.all() for all matching Modules.
See Actors and Modules for script paths and attachment.
Find UI controls
ui.find("health_text") uses the control's script key, not its display name. No match returns nil. ui.get("health_text") reports an error instead.
Use ui.find("hud", "health_text") to supply a document key. It must match the document loaded for Play.
Reference
See project lookups, global find, Cell lookup, and UI lookup.
NextEvents

entries.title: Functions
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Functions
Functions 
Write code once. Call it when you need it.
Declare a function
Declare a function with fn. Give it a name, inputs, and a body.
fn add(a: number, b: number): number {
return a + b
}
Here, a and b are the inputs. The : number after the parentheses describes the return value.
Call a function
Use the function name followed by parentheses.
const total = add(10, 20)
debug.log(total)
This prints 30. Writing add without parentheses refers to the function. It does not call it.
Parameters and return values
Parameters are local to the function. Pass one value for each required parameter.
return sends a value to the caller and ends the function. A function that ends without returning a value returns nil.
Types can be left out:
fn double(value) {
return value * 2
}
debug.log(double(5))
Functions as values
You can store a function in a variable and call it later.
const double = fn(value) {
return value * 2
}
debug.log(double(5))
Closures
A function can keep access to variables from where it was created. This is called a closure.
fn make_counter() {
count: number = 0
return fn() {
count += 1
return count
}
}
const next = make_counter()
debug.log(next())
debug.log(next())
This prints 1, then 2. Each call to make_counter() creates its own counter.
Callbacks
A callback is a function that another system calls for you. For a button example, see UI. For contact callbacks, see Events.
Functions in Modules
A Module lets another script call your functions. See Actors and Modules. A function may also pause with wait().
NextVariables
[BETA] marks features newer than the current public release. Current release: 0.8.0.
examples:
const total = add(10, 20)
debug.log(total)

entries.title: Getting started
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Getting started
Getting started 
Write and run your first AeoScript file.
Write a script
Create a file under scripts/ in your project. Use the .aeo extension.
debug.log("Game script loaded")
Top-level code runs when the script starts. This example does not need an entity declaration or an object binding.
Run it
Start Play mode. Open Output and look for Game script loaded.
If it does not appear, check that the file is saved and enabled. Read the first error in Output before changing more code.
Add a function
Learn how to declare and call functions. Use variables to keep values in the same script.
Choose a script style
Use a top-level script for game-wide setup. Use an Actor-attached Module for behavior belonging to one Actor. Use an Entity script when you need the Entity lifecycle.

entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Names and IDs
Names and IDs 
Choose names for discovery and IDs for exact objects.
Names can be shared
Names help you find objects. They do not have to be unique.
Use a plural lookup when more than one result is valid. Use a distinct name when a script expects one object.
IDs identify objects
Cell IDs and Actor IDs identify authored objects. Entity IDs identify live runtime Entities. Do not use an Actor ID with entity.get().
Bindings use authored IDs rather than names. See Script bindings.
UI keys
UI script keys are separate from display names. See UI lookup.
For all lookup choices, see Finding Objects.

entries.title: Input
Maps
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Maps
Maps 
Store values by key.
Add and read values
const values = {}
values["name"] = "Ghost"
values[1] = "First"
debug.log(values["name"])
String and numeric keys are different. values[1] and values["1"] are separate entries.
Missing keys
Reading a missing key returns nil.
if values["health"] == nil {
values["health"] = 100
}
Remove a key
Assign nil to remove an entry.
values["name"] = nil
Maps use indexing and assignment. There is no separate map namespace.
Shared state
Keep game state in a map when it needs named fields. To save supported values between game sessions, see Save data.

entries.title: Actors and Modules
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Actors and Modules
Actors and Modules 
Attach behavior to an Actor or share functions between scripts.
Call a Module
Put a helper file under scripts/.
// scripts/math_helpers.aeo
fn add(a, b) {
return a + b
}
Load it from another script:
const helper = scripts.math_helpers.aeo
debug.log(helper.add(10, 20))
Different Module files keep separate state. Reusing the same Module path reuses its state for the current game session.
Attach a Module to an Actor
Attach the script under the Actor in the project hierarchy. Inside the attached Module, self.parent is that Actor.
const actor = self.parent
actor.on_touch = fn(thing) {
debug.log("Touched by:", thing)
}
The same file attached to two Actors keeps separate state for each Actor. A standalone Module has no Actor parent; reading self.parent there reports an error.
Player Modules
Files in playerscripts/ attach to the Player. Use player.controller or player.find("Inventory") to reach them. There is no playerscripts language namespace.
Waiting in attached Modules [BETA]
Attached Modules can pause and resume while keeping their Actor parent. This behavior is repaired in the v0.8.1 development series.
For lookup details, see the Project and Module reference.

entries.title: Operators
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Operators
Operators 
Calculate, compare, and combine values.
Arithmetic
Use +, -, *, /, and % with numbers.
const total = 10 + 5 * 2
debug.log(total)
This prints 20. Parentheses change the order: (10 + 5) * 2 is 30.
Comparisons
Use ==, !=, <, <=, >, and >= to compare values.
Logic
Use && for both conditions, || for either, and ! for not.
if health > 0 && ready {
debug.log("Can act")
}
Assignment
score = 10
score += 5
See Variables for scope and constants.

entries.title: Play-mode changes
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Play-mode changes
Play-mode changes 
Understand what resets when Play stops.
Saved World and active game
The saved World is your authored content. Play starts an active game from it.
Ordinary script changes to Cells and Actors affect that game session. Stopping Play discards temporary changes.
Temporary objects
Cells created with cell.new() and controls created with ui.new() are temporary. Deleting an authored Cell during Play does not delete it from the saved World.
Keep progress [BETA]
Use Save data for supported values that must survive a restart. Do not treat a changed World object or a Module variable as a durable save.
PreviousNames and IDs

entries.title: Save data
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Save data
Save data [BETA]
Keep supported game values between sessions.
Read a value
const visits = save.get("visits")
if visits == nil {
save.set("visits", 1)
} else {
save.set("visits", visits + 1)
}
save.commit()
A missing key returns nil.
Commit changes
save.set() and save.remove() change values in memory. Call save.commit() to write them to disk. A failed commit reports an error.
Supported values
Save numbers, booleans, and strings. Baskets, maps, functions, and object handles are not supported save values.
Save data belongs to the project and uses one default slot. It does not change the saved World or script files.
See the Save API for exact calls.

Docs / AeoScript / Script control
Script control 
Enable or disable scripts during the game.
Disable a script
script.disable("scripts/example.aeo")
Disabling stops active execution and removes dynamic callbacks owned by that script. Paused calls are cancelled.
It does not delete the script file or its saved binding.
Enable a script
script.enable("scripts/example.aeo")
Use the project-relative path, including scripts/ or playerscripts/ and the .aeo extension.
Check state
debug.log(script.is_enabled("scripts/example.aeo"))
Script control and in-game tests are separate APIs. See the Script reference and Test reference.

entries.title: Syntax
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Syntax
Syntax 
Read and write AeoScript statements.
Statements and blocks
Use braces for function bodies, conditions, loops, and events.
// A comment
health: number = 100
if health > 0 {
debug.log("Alive")
}
Calls
Use parentheses for arguments. Use a dot for a namespace or object member.
debug.log("Hello")
math.clamp(health, 0, 100)
See Functions for declarations and return values.
Collections
Use square brackets for a basket and indexing. Use braces for an empty map.
const items = ["Key", "Map"]
const values = {}
values["first"] = items[0]
Other syntax
See Control flow, Operators, and Events for their syntax. There is no need to learn engine internals to write these statements.
PreviousTypesNextOperators

Types 
Know what kind of value you have.
Value types
Type
Example
number
4.5
bool
true, false
string
"Ghost"

No value

[1, 2, 3]

Numbers are 64-bit floating-point values. Strings support Unicode text.

Use annotations to state what a variable or function expects.
Object handles
A handle refers to an object owned by Worldkiln. The object may be removed while you still have its handle.

entries.title: UI
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / UI
UI 
Create controls or find controls made in the editor.
Create a control
const button = ui.new("Button")
button.text = "Start"
button.position = [20, 20]
button.size = [160, 40]
button.on_click = fn() {
debug.log("Start clicked")
}
The supported types are Panel, Text, and Button. Positions and sizes use playable-viewport pixels.
Find authored controls
Set a control's Script key in the editor. Use that key in your script.
const health = ui.find("health_text")
if health != nil {
health.text = "75 / 100"
}
Keys are case-sensitive. Display names are not script keys. ui.get() reports an error if the key is missing; ui.find() returns nil.
The optional document key must match the document loaded for Play.
Anchors
Set anchor to a named point such as "TopRight". Position becomes an offset from that point.
"Stretch" uses position as left/top margins and size as right/bottom margins.
Parent controls [BETA]
Set parent to another Ui handle, or nil to use the root. A hidden or disabled parent also affects its children.
Text layout [BETA]
Text and Button controls support font size, alignment, wrapping, padding, and line spacing. See the UI reference for allowed values.
Play changes
Runtime controls and property changes do not change the saved UI document. Starting a new Play session restores authored values.
PreviousLive EntitiesNextInput

entries.title: Variables
entries.body:
Docs / AeoScript / Variables
Variables 
Keep a value and use it later.
Set a value
score = 0
score += 10
debug.log(score)
This prints 10. You can give a variable a type:
health: number = 100
name: string = "Ada"
ready: bool = true
Constants
Use const when the variable should not be assigned again.
const max_health = 100
A constant basket can still have its contents changed. Use basket.freeze() to make its contents read-only.
Scope
Top-level variables are available to functions and event handlers in the same script. Function parameters and local variables belong to their function.
Separate Module files keep separate state. Actor-attached Modules also keep state for each Actor. See Modules.
No value
Use nil for no value. Check a lookup result before reading its properties. See Finding Objects.
PreviousFunctionsNextControl flow

Waiting 
Pause a script and continue where it stopped.
Pause for a time
debug.log("Starting")

Wait inside a function

Disabling the script cancels its active work. It will not resume the paused call. See Script control.

Engine host 
How scripts reach engine-owned objects.
Handles
A handle stores the kind and ID of an engine-owned object. It does not own the object. The object can disappear while the handle remains.

The scripting API validates calls and routes them through the engine host. The host reads or changes the active game state.
Keep authored IDs and runtime IDs distinct. Use tests to check invalid handles and unsupported object kinds.

Docs / Documentation / Persistence
Persistence [BETA]
Keep authored content, runtime changes, and save data separate.
Authored data
World and project files store authored content. Ordinary Play changes must not rewrite those files.
Runtime state
Play keeps temporary overrides and objects. Stopping Play discards them.
Save data
The save service stores supported typed values in a project-specific application-data location. Set and remove operations are staged until an explicit commit.
Commits replace a versioned save document atomically. Newer unsupported formats must be rejected rather than rewritten.

Physics architecture 
How simulation and script controls fit together.
Simulation
Physics runs simulation steps for bodies, Characters, and collision. Rendering and script calls do not define the physics timestep.
Script controls
Scripts set intent or use supported physics controls. The engine owns gravity, collision, and body movement.
Contact events enter the script event queue. Check the object type supplied by each contact path when changing callback behavior.

Test solid and trigger contacts separately. Test both Character-to-Cell and Entity-to-Entity contacts.

entries.title: Runtime and waiting
entries.body:
Docs / Documentation / Runtime and waiting
Runtime and waiting 
How Worldkiln runs and pauses script work.
Script work
Worldkiln runs script work through resumable tasks called fibers. Each task keeps its call stack and local values.
wait() pauses the current task. The scheduler resumes it later while other game systems continue running.
Instances
An instance owns script state. Entity lifecycle calls and Actor-attached Modules use their own instances. Sharing compiled code must not share instance state.
Contributor checks
Changes to waiting must preserve local values, nested calls, and Actor Module parents. Use regression tests for those cases.
For script authors, see Waiting and Modules.

entries.title: Script errors
entries.body:
Docs / Documentation / Script errors
Script errors 
Fix the first error, then run the script again.
Unknown name
Check spelling and scope. A function must be declared or loaded from the right Module. See Functions and Modules.
No lookup result
Check the object type before changing its name. proj.find() does not find Cells. ui.find() uses a Script key. See Finding Objects.
Invalid handle
The object may have been destroyed. Check its validity before using it again, especially after wait().
Wrong arguments
Open the exact entry in the API reference. Check the number of arguments, their types, and any required handle kind.
Execution limit
A loop must finish or pause. Replace repeated polling with an event when possible. See Control flow.
Lifecycle does not run
Lifecycle functions need a matching object attachment. For a startup message, use top-level code. See Bindings.
More useful error locations [BETA]
The v0.8.2 development series adds clearer script, line, and function information, including errors inside Module calls.

Make a timed Block 
Create a Block, then remove it after a delay.
Create the script
This exercise combines temporary Cells and waiting. Save it as scripts/timed_block.aeo:
const block = cell.new("Block")
block.position = [5, 2, 5]
block.color = [1, 0.5, 0]
wait(2.0)
cell.delete(block)
debug.log("Block removed")
Check the result
Start Play. Look at the Block before two seconds pass. It should disappear and Output should show Block removed.
Use an open position in your World so the Block is visible. This is a small scripting exercise; it does not create a complete game.
Continue
Read Waiting to understand the pause. Use Events when an action should happen after player input or contact.
